report.source_text: She underwent embolisation with access via the left common femoral artery. There was a small distal right superior rectal AVM with filling of a large right rectal haemorrhoid. This was microcanulated to within 1 cm of the fistula point and embolised with 0.1 mL of N-butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) lipiodol. A flexible sigmoidoscopy a few days later demonstrated no features of recent haemorrhage, and a proctoscopy visualised a moderate sized internal haemorrhoid at 7 o'clock which was banded without complications. She was discharged home the next day.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old female presented with a 2-day history of per rectal bleeding and mild mid abdominal discomfort without prior trauma or relevant family history. A contrast-enhanced pelvic CT mesenteric angiogram demonstrated prominent serpiginous vessels with right-sided predominance involving the pelvis, highly suggestive of a pelvic AVM, and no active gastrointestinal hemorrhage. She underwent embolisation of a right superior rectal AVM and banding of a moderate sized internal hemorrhoid. Post-procedure flexible sigmoidoscopy showed no recent hemorrhage, and she was discharged. A repeat CTMA one month later showed diminished rectal AVM component but persistent draining veins, consistent with partial response.
